title: Rained Off
setting: A Sunday evening. Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, leaves a voicemail for Kenta, who lent him a tent for a camping trip with some old friends. Rain spoiled part of their plan, and Satou-san has an idea for next Saturday.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, kenta-kun? satou desu. tento, kashite kurete arigatou gozaimashita.
lines.ja: もしもし、ケンタくん？佐藤です。テント、貸してくれてありがとうございました。
lines.kana: もしもし、けんたくん？さとうです。てんと、かしてくれてありがとうございました。
lines.english: Hello, Kenta? It's Satou. Thank you for lending me your tent.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kinou kara, mukashi no tomodachi to kyanpu ni itteta n desu. sakki kaette kimashita.
lines.ja: 昨日から、昔の友達とキャンプに行ってたんです。さっき帰ってきました。
lines.kana: きのうから、むかしのともだちときゃんぷにいってたんです。さっきかえってきました。
lines.english: I've been away camping with some old friends since yesterday. I just got back.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hontou wa, kinou minna de yama ni noboru tsumori datta n desu kedo, ame de dame deshita.
lines.ja: 本当は、昨日みんなで山に登るつもりだったんですけど、雨でだめでした。
lines.kana: ほんとうは、きのうみんなでやまにのぼるつもりだったんですけど、あめでだめでした。
lines.english: We'd actually planned to climb a mountain together yesterday, but the rain put a stop to that.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sorede, kawari ni tsuri ni itta n desu. maa, nanimo tsuremasen deshita kedo ne.
lines.ja: それで、代わりに釣りに行ったんです。まあ、何も釣れませんでしたけどね。
lines.kana: それで、かわりにつりにいったんです。まあ、なにもつれませんでしたけどね。
lines.english: So we went fishing instead. Not that we caught a thing.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: demo, minna de zutto hanashitete, ii kibun tenkan ni narimashita yo.
lines.ja: でも、みんなでずっと話してて、いい気分転換になりましたよ。
lines.kana: でも、みんなでずっとはなしてて、いいきぶんてんかんになりましたよ。
lines.english: But we chatted the whole time, and it made a really nice change of pace.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sou ieba kenta-kun, mou sannen mo kyanpu ni ittenai tte, ittemashita yo ne.
lines.ja: そういえばケンタくん、もう三年もキャンプに行ってないって、言ってましたよね。
lines.kana: そういえばけんたくん、もうさんねんもきゃんぷにいってないって、いってましたよね。
lines.english: Come to think of it, Kenta, you told me you hadn't been camping in three whole years.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: saikin wa shigoto bakkari de, zenzen karada o ugokashitenai tte.
lines.ja: 最近は仕事ばっかりで、全然体を動かしてないって。
lines.kana: さいきんはしごとばっかりで、ぜんぜんからだをうごかしてないって。
lines.english: And that lately it's been all work, and you haven't been moving your body at all.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: raishuu no doyoubi, minna de mou ichido, ano yama ni noboru n desu. kenta-kun mo issho ni dou desu ka?
lines.ja: 来週の土曜日、みんなでもう一度、あの山に登るんです。ケンタくんも一緒にどうですか？
lines.kana: らいしゅうのどようび、みんなでもういちど、あのやまにのぼるんです。けんたくんもいっしょにどうですか？
lines.english: Next Saturday we're all having another go at that mountain. Why don't you come along?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: chiisai yama desu kara, toshi o totta watashi demo noboremasu. demo, chanto karada o ugokasemasu yo.
lines.ja: 小さい山ですから、年をとった私でも登れます。でも、ちゃんと体を動かせますよ。
lines.kana: ちいさいやまですから、としをとったわたしでものぼれます。でも、ちゃんとからだをうごかせますよ。
lines.english: It's a small one, so even an old man like me can climb it. But you'll still get some proper exercise.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: shigoto de sutoresu mo tamatteru deshou? tama ni wa kibun tenkan shinai to.
lines.ja: 仕事でストレスもたまってるでしょう？たまには気分転換しないと。
lines.kana: しごとですとれすもたまってるでしょう？たまにはきぶんてんかんしないと。
lines.english: Work must be getting you stressed, too. You need a change of pace now and then.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: yama ni nobotte kara, mata tsuri ni iku tsumori desu. sore mo ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu yo.
lines.ja: 山に登ってから、また釣りに行くつもりです。それもいい気分転換になりますよ。
lines.kana: やまにのぼってから、またつりにいくつもりです。それもいいきぶんてんかんになりますよ。
lines.english: After the climb, we're planning to go fishing again. That'll do you good, too.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: a, doyoubi wa asa yoji ni demasu kara ne. jaa, renraku mattemasu.
lines.ja: あ、土曜日は朝四時に出ますからね。じゃあ、連絡待ってます。
lines.kana: あ、どようびはあさよじにでますからね。じゃあ、れんらくまってます。
lines.english: Oh, and on Saturday we leave at four in the morning. Well, let me know.

questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、どうしてケンタくんに電話しましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、どうしてけんたくんにでんわしましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, doushite kenta-kun ni denwa shimashita ka?

choices.english: To say the rain spoiled the whole trip, so he's bringing the tent back and staying home next weekend.
To thank him for the tent and invite him to climb the mountain with them next Saturday, after rain stopped them this time.
To tell him they caught lots of fish, and ask him to come fishing with them early tomorrow morning.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Satou-san thanks Kenta for lending him the tent. Lines 3-4: rain stopped them climbing the mountain, so they went fishing instead. Line 8: they're all having another go at that mountain next Saturday, and he asks Kenta to come, since Kenta said he hadn't been getting any exercise (line 7). A is wrong: the rain only stopped the climb, the trip was still a nice change of pace (line 5), and he's going out again next Saturday and wants Kenta along. C is wrong: they didn't catch a thing (line 4), and the outing is next Saturday, leaving at four in the morning (line 12), not tomorrow.

questions.english: Your friend Sora has spent all Sunday indoors. In the evening he stretches and groans, "kyou mo zutto uchi de geemu shiteta. nanka karada ga darui naa." Tell him he needs to get some exercise now and then, using karada o ugokasu.
questions.ja: 今日もずっとうちでゲームしてた。なんか体がだるいなあ。
questions.kana: きょうもずっとうちでげーむしてた。なんかからだがだるいなあ。
questions.romaji: kyou mo zutto uchi de geemu shiteta. nanka karada ga darui naa.
questions.answer: Tell him to get moving: tama ni wa karada (o) ugokasanakya (you've got to get some exercise now and then), or suggest doing it together with karada o ugokasou. It's ugokasu, with o.

modelAnswers.romaji: zutto uchi ni iru kara da yo. tama ni wa karada ugokasanakya.
modelAnswers.ja: ずっとうちにいるからだよ。たまには体動かさなきゃ。
modelAnswers.english: That's because you've been stuck indoors all day. You've got to get some exercise now and then.

modelAnswers.romaji: ashita, issho ni soto de karada o ugokasou yo. sukoshi demo zenzen chigau kara.
modelAnswers.ja: 明日、一緒に外で体を動かそうよ。少しでも全然違うから。
modelAnswers.english: Let's go out and get some exercise together tomorrow. Even a little makes a big difference.

questions.explanation: Satou-san reminds Kenta he said he hadn't been moving his body at all (zenzen karada o ugokashitenai, line 7), and promises the small mountain still gives a proper workout (chanto karada o ugokasemasu, line 9). karada o ugokasu is the everyday way to talk about getting exercise, anything from a walk to a climb, and casual speech often drops the o (karada ugokasanakya). ugokasu means move something, so it takes o; ugoku is move by itself, so karada o ugoku is wrong, and karada ga ugokanai means you physically can't move. undou suru (exercise) works too, but it leans towards sport and the gym.

questions.english: Your manager Tanaka-san looks worn out on Friday afternoon and says, "saikin isogashikute, shuumatsu mo shigoto no koto bakari kangaete shimau n desu yo." Suggest something for the weekend and tell him it'll do him good, using kibun tenkan ni naru.
questions.ja: 最近忙しくて、週末も仕事のことばかり考えてしまうんですよ。
questions.kana: さいきんいそがしくて、しゅうまつもしごとのことばかりかんがえてしまうんですよ。
questions.romaji: saikin isogashikute, shuumatsu mo shigoto no koto bakari kangaete shimau n desu yo.
questions.answer: Suggest an outing (tsuri ni itte mitara dou desu ka?) and add ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu yo (it'd be a nice change of pace). Keep it polite with Tanaka-san: narimasu, not naru.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, shuumatsu wa tsuri ni itte mitara dou desu ka? ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、週末は釣りに行ってみたらどうですか？いい気分転換になりますよ。
modelAnswers.english: Then why not try going fishing this weekend? It'd be a nice change of pace.

modelAnswers.romaji: tama ni wa yama ni nobotte mitara dou desu ka? kitto ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: たまには山に登ってみたらどうですか？きっといい気分転換になりますよ。
modelAnswers.english: How about climbing a mountain for once? I'm sure it'd do you good.

questions.explanation: Satou-san says the rained-off trip still made ii kibun tenkan ni narimashita (a nice change of pace, line 5), and that fishing after the climb will be ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu too (line 11). kibun tenkan ni naru, usually with ii, says something does you good as a break, which makes it the natural phrase for encouraging someone. kibun tenkan suru is taking the break yourself: in line 10 Satou-san tells Kenta tama ni wa kibun tenkan shinai to (you need to take a break now and then). kibarashi ni naru works the same way, but leans towards taking your mind off something bad.

questions.english: On Monday your friend Yuki says, "shuumatsu, nani shiteta no? zutto renraku nakatta kedo." You didn't answer because you were climbing a mountain with friends on Saturday. Tell her, using yama ni noboru.
questions.ja: 週末、何してたの？ずっと連絡なかったけど。
questions.kana: しゅうまつ、なにしてたの？ずっとれんらくなかったけど。
questions.romaji: shuumatsu, nani shiteta no? zutto renraku nakatta kedo.
questions.answer: Say you were up a mountain with friends: tomodachi to yama ni nobotteta (n da), or yama ni nobotta. Keep the ni.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen gomen, tomodachi to yama ni nobotteta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめんごめん、友達と山に登ってたんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, sorry! I was off climbing a mountain with some friends.

modelAnswers.romaji: doyoubi ni, tomodachi to yama ni nobotta n da. ue made sanjikan mo kakatta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 土曜日に、友達と山に登ったんだ。上まで三時間もかかったよ。
modelAnswers.english: I climbed a mountain with friends on Saturday. It took three whole hours to reach the top.

questions.explanation: Satou-san had planned yama ni noboru tsumori (line 3), says they'll climb ano yama ni noboru next Saturday (line 8), and plans to go fishing again yama ni nobotte kara (after the climb, line 11). English 'climb a mountain' pulls you towards yama o noboru, which is also heard when the way up is the point (a steep path), but for having been up a mountain ni is about three times as common. noboremasu in line 9 is the can-do form: toshi o totta watashi demo noboremasu, even an old man like me can climb it. nobotteta is 'was climbing', a natural excuse for not answering.

questions.english: When rain stopped the climb, what did Satou-san and his friends do instead?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんたちは、代わりに何をしましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんたちは、かわりになにをしましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san-tachi wa, kawari ni nani o shimashita ka?

choices.english: They climbed a smaller mountain nearby.
They went fishing and caught enough for dinner.
They went fishing, but nobody caught anything.

questions.explanation: Line 4: sorede, kawari ni tsuri ni itta n desu (so we went fishing instead), then nanimo tsuremasen deshita (we didn't catch a thing). tsuri ni iku puts the activity straight before ni iku, and tsureru is a fish getting caught on the line, so the negative means nothing bit. B misses that negative. A: nobody climbed anything; rain called off the climb (line 3), and they'll try the same mountain next Saturday (line 8), with fishing again afterwards (mata tsuri ni iku tsumori, line 11).

questions.english: What did Satou-san say Kenta hadn't done for three years?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、ケンタくんのことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、けんたくんのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, kenta-kun no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: He hasn't been camping in three whole years.
choices.romaji: mou sannen mo kyanpu ni ittenai

choices.english: He hasn't gone 'camping' in three whole years (the English -ing word).
choices.romaji: mou sannen mo kyanpingu ni ittenai

choices.english: He hasn't been fishing in three whole years.
choices.romaji: mou sannen mo tsuri ni ittenai

questions.explanation: Line 6: sou ieba kenta-kun, mou sannen mo kyanpu ni ittenai tte, ittemashita yo ne. ittenai is itte (i)nai, haven't gone, and Satou-san says the same of his own trip in line 2: kyanpu ni itteta n desu (I was away camping). B copies the English '-ing': the activity is kyanpu, and kyanpingu turns up mostly in compounds like kyanpingu kaa (camper van). C: fishing is what Satou-san did on his trip and plans for next Saturday; what Kenta hadn't done in three years was camp, which is why his tent was free to lend.

newWords.english: (of a fish) be caught, bite: nanimo tsuremasen deshita = we didn't catch a thing
name suffix for a younger man or boy (kenta-kun)
